data.description: If the bank answered accept/reject AND handed the note back, you could probe each qubit until you learn it, then print perfect copies.

single_copy_pass.label: One counterfeit passes
single_copy_pass.note: the forged copies are identical; reported jointly

counterfeit_success.label: Both counterfeits pass (exact)
counterfeit_success.note: success of ONE specific attack: a LOWER bound on worst-case counterfeiting, never an upper bound

theorem_bound.label: Theorem bound
theorem_bound.note: OUT_OF_MODEL: W1 forbids verifier-oracle access, so (3/4)^n does not apply

hardware.label: Quantum hardware
hardware.note: not run: paid hardware submission is disabled in this build (lane J); no QPU number exists

assumptions: one genuine note; the counterfeiter returns two candidate notes; the bank verifies both in the secret bases
Monte Carlo draws a FRESH secret note per trial (never repeated shots of one note)
W1 value (3/4)^n = 0.177979 shown for contrast only
data.simulator_caveat: A simulator's state is classical data that can be copied freely; nothing here demonstrates physical no-cloning. Only the modelled quantum register is simulated.
